Internal Family Systems (IFS) was developed by Richard Schwartz, who arrived at
it while working with families and finding that his patients described the same
dynamics happening inside one person. Its starting position is that a mind is
made of **parts** rather than a single voice, that having parts is the normal
condition rather than a pathology, and that every part is attempting to protect
you even when what it does causes harm.

## Concepts

- **The Self.** The seat of awareness underneath the parts, taken to be
  undamaged whatever has happened. It is recognised by calm, curiosity and
  compassion, and the work of the method is to get it into the room rather than
  to install it.
- **Exiles.** The young parts carrying the pain of what happened, pushed out of
  awareness because feeling them was unbearable at the time.
- **Managers.** Protectors working in advance, arranging life so that nothing
  reaches an exile. Perfectionism, criticism and caretaking are typical jobs.
- **Firefighters.** Protectors working after the fact, acting once an exile
  breaks through. Numbing, bingeing and rage are typical, and they accept
  damage as the price of stopping the pain.
- **No bad parts.** A destructive behaviour is read as a protective role that
  has no better option available. The question asked of a part is what it is
  afraid would happen if it stopped.
- **Unblending.** Separating from a part so you are *with* it instead of
  *being* it, which is what makes the rest possible.
- **Unburdening.** A part can hand back the belief or emotion it took on from
  an event, and take up a different role afterwards.
